topics.chapterTitle: Understanding CPU Architecture for C++ Performance
topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: Modern processors execute source code through several layers of translation, scheduling, caching, and speculation. A useful performance model identifies dependencies and data movement without pretending that every processor shares the same pipeline or cache geometry. This chapter compares one long dependency chain with several independent accumulators while keeping the numerical result exact for the chosen input.

topics.title: 15.1.1 Understanding Instruction-Level Parallelism
topics.summary: Independent instructions can overlap in execution when the processor and generated code permit it. A reduction that repeatedly updates one accumulator creates a dependency chain; multiple partial accumulators can expose independent work before a final combination.

topics.chapterTitle: Understanding CPU Architecture for C++ Performance
topics.title: 15.1.2 Understanding Out-of-Order Execution
topics.summary: Many high-performance CPUs can schedule ready operations before earlier stalled operations while preserving required architectural behavior. This can hide some latency when independent work is available. It cannot remove true data dependencies or make an invalid data race legal.

blocks.text: C++ ordering rules, compiler reordering, and processor execution are distinct layers. Synchronization must be expressed using the language’s atomics or locks, not by assuming source order becomes a fixed instruction schedule. A performance explanation should not turn an observed processor behavior into a portability guarantee.

topics.title: 15.2.1 Understanding CPU Cache Levels
topics.summary: Caches retain recently used memory blocks closer to execution resources. Their sizes, associativity, sharing, and line geometry vary by processor. Contiguous access often uses fetched data efficiently, while pointer chasing can make each next address depend on a prior load.

topics.title: 15.2.2 Understanding Main-Memory Latency
topics.summary: A cache miss can require access to a more distant cache or main memory, with latency affected by contention, topology, and access pattern. Multiple outstanding requests can improve throughput, but a dependent pointer chain may expose latency directly because the next address is not known yet.

topics.chapterTitle: Understanding CPU Architecture for C++ Performance
topics.title: Solution and review notes
topics.summary: Independent accumulators break arithmetic dependencies, not address dependencies. In a linked traversal, the next pointer may require the current load to complete, leaving less independent work to overlap. A contiguous representation or batched traversal can change that structure more fundamentally.
